full_judgment:
The ACC issued notice on 18-02-2007 under section 26(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 read with Rule 15 gha (1) and (5) of the Emergency Powers Rules, 2007 under the signature of its Secretary, an Officer of the Commission, directing the respondent No.1 in jail custody, to submit statement of assets and liabilities in his own and dependants name within 72 hours which he duly complied with by submission of the statement. The Investigation Officer after completion of the investigation, submitted charge sheet to the appropriate Court along with necessary sanction for trial. During the trial, this review petitioner, examined 37 PWs and the defence. examined 7 DWs and the Court of Special Judge having taken into consideration the law and facts of the case and weighing all evidence specially, the legality of issuing of the notice with satisfaction of the Secretary, an Officer of the Commission, under Rule 15 gha (1) and (2) of the EPR, 2007 passed the judgment and order of conviction arid sentence by applying special rules of evidence i.e. presumption of guilt against the accused under section 27(2) of ACC Act and section 7 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act meaning that the accused is to rebut the presumption of guilt against him up to the Court's satisfaction. 

 34. He also submits that this Court ought to consider that the offence for possessing assets disproportionate to his legitimate sources of income stands proved under section 27(1) of the ACC Act which has got nothing to do with the notice/order dated 18-2-2007 issued by the Secretary of the Commission inasmuch as the appellant-respondent No.1 failed to rebut presumption of the trial court under section 27(2) of the ACC Act, section 5(3) of the Prevention of Corruption Act and section 7(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, and hence, the High Court Division has fallen into serious error of facts and law. 

 47. In order to address and consider the foregoing issues and questions of law and fact we have to examine firstly, the facts, circumstances and the laws involved in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 giving rise to Criminal Review Petition No. 18 of 2010. The prosecution Case, in short, is that the ACC issued notice on 18-2-2007 under section 26( 1) of the ACC Act, 2004 read with Rule 15 gha (1) and (5) of the EPR, 2007 under the signature of its Secretary, an Officer of the Commission, ordering the respondent No.1 in jail custody, to submit statement of assets and liabilities in his own and dependents’ name within 72 hours which he duly complied with by submission of the statement. The Investigation Officer after completion of the investigation, submitted charge sheet to the appropriate Court along with necessary sanction for trial. During the trial, this review petitioner examined 37 PWs and the defence examined 7 DWs. The learned Special Judge, Special Court No.3, Dhaka in Special Case No. 1 of 2007 on completion of the trial having taken into consideration of the laws and facts of the case and materials on record and weighing all evidence specially, the legality of issuance of the order with satisfaction of the Secretary, an Officer of the Commission, under Rule 15 gha (1) and (5) of the EPR, 2007 passed the judgment and order dated 26-7-2007 by applying special rules of evidence i.e .. presumption of guilt against the accused under section 27(2) of ACC Act and section 7 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act meaning that the accused is to rebut the presumption of guilt against him up to the Court's satisfaction, convicted and sentenced the respondent No.1 to suffer simple imprisonment for three years under section 26(2) of the Act read with Rule 15 gha (S) of the EPR, 2007 and rigorous imprisonment for 10 years under section 27(1) of the ACC Act and to pay a fine of Taka 10,00,000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more and also forfeited his properties.
